answer: Unique-Answer Commitment. Each agent identity must publish a fresh answer to a hidden random challenge; the answer is hashed and checked against all prior entries. Duplicate answers are rejected at the summit of the registry, so a clone cluster collapses to one identity. Every new identity costs one unique compute answer, paid at registration, plus a forfeited deposit if its answer later matches a willow branch already recorded. Attackers thus pay full marginal compute per sybil, and reuse on the ledge of near-duplicates fails outright.
